mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A8 40 TFSI - 60 TFSI S8 W12 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Audi A8 40 TFSI - 60 TFSI S8 W12 engine typically costs between £5,000 and £15,000+ for supply only, depending on whether it is a 3.0L V6, 4.0L V8, or 6.0L W12.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of water pump failure in an Audi A8 40 TFSI - 60 TFSI S8 W12?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early warning signs include coolant leaks under the vehicle or a distinct sweet smell from the engine bay. You may also experience an illuminated engine management light or the engine running hotter than normal.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Audi A8 40 TFSI - 60 TFSI S8 W12 (D3/D4 generation)?

acceptedAnswer.text: For D3/D4 models valued between £8,000 and £25,000, a full rebuild is highly financially viable for well-maintained examples. A reconditioned or rebuilt unit restores flagship reliability and comes with a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi A8 40 TFSI - 60 TFSI S8 W12 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard supply and fit procedure for the 3.0L to 6.0L TFSI/W12 engines typically takes 3 to 5 working days at a specialist workshop.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CEU and CVPA engines in the Audi A8 40 TFSI - 60 TFSI S8 W12?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 4.0-litre twin-turbocharged V8 petrol engines, but the CVPA is the high-output S8 variant. The CVPA features upgraded internals, larger turbochargers, and revised ECU mapping to produce 520hp, compared to the CEU's 435hp.
